records.text: Swamp Gas is a gas cloud.

K. Lee Smallfry is a master engineering trainer and repair worker at Telredor, where she needs spare parts for a broken compression coil and other repairs. She is intrigued by swamp gas and offers plans for a Zapthrottle Mote Extractor in exchange for parts. When shown a strange engine part, she calls it special, suspects it may have fallen from the sky, and asks that the matter stay between you. Her charming smile and delight in strawberries add a playful note to her practical, curious manner.

Mack Diver is a master engineering trainer in Zabra'jin. His work includes the Zapthrottle Mote Extractor: he asks for parts from a broken steam pump in the Dead Mire before sharing the schematics, and jokes that he has diving to do.

Watcher Leesa'oh studies the sporelings and their relationships with Zangarmarsh’s other creatures through careful observation. Alarmed that hungry bog lords may wipe out the sporelings by eating their pods, she investigates their changing diet and works on growing mushrooms as an alternative food source. Buddy, her beloved, scratch-prone cat, accompanies her; she affectionately calls him along to see whether the plan works.

Lethyn Moonfire is a Cenarion druid concerned with keeping Zangarmarsh’s ecosystem in balance. Lethyn treats the aggressive, unusually fast-growing marshtrekker Boglash as a symptom of that imbalance and asks allies to investigate it. Lethyn also directs a check on the Cenarion druids at Terokkar’s Cenarion Thicket after they stop reporting in.

Ysiel Windsinger leads the Cenarion Expedition in Zangarmarsh and studies the marsh as a thriving but vulnerable ecosystem. As its water levels fall, she organises reconnaissance to trace the depletion and determine how widely the naga are involved; she uses druidic magic to shape a scout for the task. After learning that the naga drain Serpent Lake, she sends druids to investigate, then seeks help when they fail to return.

Gzhun'tt is a Sporeggar sporeling concerned with his people's survival and peaceful relations. The marsh's lowered water levels have made sanguine hibiscus scarce, leaving Sporeggar short of a flower they use for several purposes. He also seeks allies against Bloodscale naga attacks on his people, hoping to make the naga think twice about further harassment.

T'shu is a Sporeggar sporeling with a mischievous streak in the conflict with the spore giants. He wants a frond stolen from the prized Underspore plant tended by Hungerfen, believing the theft will damage the giants' morale. He jokes that the giants might instead become so angry that they attack Sporeggar again, and shrugs at the risk.

Warden Hamoot is responsible for security at the Cenarion Expedition, where he expected the wardens to face opposition but was surprised by the naga’s strength and numbers. After their attacks made a peaceful mission impossible, he organized resistance and declared a bounty on Darkcrest leader Rajah Haghazed. He speaks bluntly about his dislike of naga and shows little regret when they are killed.

Khn'nix speaks for the Sporeggar against the marsh walkers, an ancestral danger to his people. With spore giants creating new problems, he fears another attack and sends a capable ally after the Black Stalker, the brood’s great mother. He takes no ordinary pleasure in killing, but the suffering her brood has caused leaves him relieved by her death. He expects another offspring to replace her eventually, so the respite will be temporary.

Fhwoor is a friend of the Sporelings, who once saved him; he insists they are friends, not food. He hates the naga and sets out to recover their ark from a nearby village for his Sporeling friends. In his simple, direct speech, he invites help, prepares to move, and exults when he can smash naga along the way.

Watcher Jhang is a Cenarion Expedition investigator at Coilfang Reservoir. After twisting their ankle, they are too weak to enter the naga stronghold, so they ask allies to find their four companions—Rayge, Bite, Greenthumb, and Claw—and identify Warlord Kalithresh as the leader directing the naga. Jhang admits their companions can be reckless, but clearly cares for them. If deaths are reported, Jhang grieves those lost.
Kameel Longstride is a stable master who offers to stable pets and help recover lost companions, including those who have gone missing.
Ashyen is an Ancient of Lore allied with the Cenarion Expedition. He offers the Mark of Lore to allies who seek his blessing, and says nature favors those willing to learn its secrets.

Keleth is an Ancient of War allied with the Cenarion Expedition, granting the Mark of War to trusted members; its boon grows with their renown. Keleth warns that those who try to subdue nature will never succeed permanently.
Fedryen Swiftspear is the Cenarion Expedition quartermaster at Cenarion Refuge. He supplies the expedition’s goods and repairs equipment.

Lauranna Thar'well is the Cenarion Expedition cataloguer, tracking Zangarmarsh plants as the lakes lose water. She studies plant parts to assess native-species decline and invasive growth, while acknowledging that she lacks enough evidence to conclude what is causing the change. She recruits help to protect the sporelings in Funggor Cavern and reviews reports of new specimens, even proposing a name for one. She says she enjoys sorting and sees understanding plants as a way to understand nature.

Fahssn speaks urgently for the Sporelings when bog lords threaten their young and community. He explains that the spore sacs are where their young come from, and asks for mature sacs to be saved from the fungal giants. He says bog lords have long been kept at bay with spears and stones, but that they have grown more aggressive or desperate. Since Sporelings are outmatched, he asks better-armed visitors to fight the bog lords and bring back tendrils as proof. He recognizes those who help and promises to tell his people of their deeds.

Msshi'fn is Sporeggar's primus and elder, responsible for ensuring the village has supplies. He explains that Sporelings trade shiny Glowcap mushrooms for food and supplies, and asks for Glowcaps to build the village's reserves. He welcomes visitors who have proved themselves helpful, while noting that outsiders are uncommon in Sporeggar. His welcome and gratitude reflect a leader mindful of his people's needs and open to a proven visitor's help.

Gshaff gathers fertile spores to help rebuild Sporeggar's supply of tallstalk mushrooms. He explains that spore bats and marsh walkers collect the spores while moving among tallstalks, and that Sporelings' short stature limits their ability to gather them. Tallstalks are vital and useful to the village, while bog lord attacks have left Sporeggar short of them. He welcomes help with the collection and says the whole community will be in the visitor's debt.
Buddy is an animal companion who follows Watcher Leesa’oh when directed.

Ikeyen escaped the Umbrafen tribe and fears its leader, Kataru, and the tribe’s slavers. The Cenarion druids shelter him; he repays them by teaching about the marsh’s plants and animals. He once hid in a cave after escaping and lost his only worldly belongings there.

Kayra Longmane is a druid who was abducted while gathering herbs near Cenarion Refuge. During her escape, she urges her rescuer onward, warns of danger, and is eager to reach the refuge and rejoin her fellow druids.

Anchorite Ahuurn was once a cloistered priest and helped turn Telredor from a shrine into a refuge for draenei. He seeks to understand and reunite the Lost Ones with the draenei, reaching out to the Feralfen through Boha'mu and Elder Kuruti. Their refusal surprises him, though he accepts their right to choose and recognizes that deceiving them was misguided.

Vindicator Idaar has lived among Telredor's anchorites and knows the marsh well. He investigates the Dead Mire's unexplained decline, testing the soil and tracing the effects on its life; he concludes the soil is depleted and that withered giants cannot be saved from their suffering. He also worries about Tuurem, his former home, and seeks news of it through a letter to Andarl.

Haalrun is a draenei alchemy supplier in Telredor and came there with Noraani; they were once the refuge’s only outsiders. Practical and resourceful, he uses local materials such as umbraglow stinger wings to waterproof supplies. He worries that new troll hunters could intensify competition for food, and notes that fish and mushrooms help sustain the refuge.

Noraani is a draenei reagent merchant in Telredor who arrived with Haalrun, when they were the refuge’s only outsiders. She welcomes newcomers and helps maintain food and supplies, following the kindness shown by the Telredor anchorites. Umbrafen eel is a staple of their diet; she also worries that marshfang rippers threaten foraging parties and hopes they will leave gatherers alone.

Ruam cultivates fulgor mushrooms to supply Telredor with light, preferring them to confining the marsh’s glowing creatures. He also investigates how the drying Dead Mire is affecting its wildlife: the withering bog giants may no longer be able to spawn, and his examination of hydra and bog lord samples points to damage spreading among creatures dependent on swampy conditions. He intends to keep monitoring the area with the Cenarion Expedition.

Ikuti is a Broken of the Kurenai, a group seeking renewed ties with draenei and their allies. His delegation at Orebor Harborage works to build those ties while defending its refuge from Ango’rosh ogres. Wary of outsiders, he welcomes shelter when Anchorite Ahuurn vouches for a visitor and hopes mutual trust will grow. Ikuti also navigates disagreements with draenei over whether to pursue Lost Ones, while opposing the Daggerfen’s violence. He remembers his former life as a draenei and expects further cooperation between the Kurenai and their allies.

Puluu is a Broken at Orebor Harborage who sees his people’s hardships as having brought them closer to the land. He values practical uses for marshlight bleeder venom, from hunting to healing, and wants to demonstrate them to the draenei at Telredor. He also works to secure routes for Kurenai messengers between Telredor and Telaar, and opposes the naga’s cruel use of slaves as bait for Terrorclaw.

Maktu is a Kurenai armor maker at Orebor Harborage. He admires the protective fenclaw hides he uses and wants to show draenei how Kurenai make armor, despite joking about their shiny gear. After a huge hydra called Mragesh nearly killed him while he hunted for hides at Serpent Lake, Maktu seeks revenge so he will not be caught off guard again. He considers Mragesh’s old hide too soft for armor.

Zurai is a merchant and outpost leader at Swamprat Post, sent by Shadow Hunter Denjai with builders and warriors to establish it. He keeps Denjai informed, worries about missing scout Jyoba, and organizes precautions after learning of the Dead Mire danger. Between patrols, he replaces his mail with hydra scales suited to the marsh.

Reavij helps defend Swamprat Post against marshfangs, though he finds the swamp unpleasant and would prefer a better location to Denjai's temper. He is courting Magasha despite knowing she favors Zurai, and believes proving his hunting skill will win her over. After his charms fail, he angrily dismisses Witch Doctor Tor'gash's advice.

Shadow Hunter Denjai commands the Darkspear forces in Zangarmarsh and oversees Zabra'jin. He watches for threats to the outpost: he suspects nearby Ango'rosh activity may signal an attack, worries about ogres filtering down from the northern mountains, and says Daggerfen attacks have cost scouts and messengers while threatening the roads. He sent Zurai to establish a presence on the eastern border and expects reports from him.

Witch Doctor Tor'gash reads omens with Burstcap mushrooms, which he says are nearly gone and dangerous without precautions. He has an eccentric plan to introduce murlocs to the Lost Ones by releasing young ones from a cage near Daggerfen Village; he is protective of his baby murlocs and jokes that he has sharp eyes and mighty ears.

Gambarinka is a tradesman whose work in Zabra’jin is disrupted by the marshlight bleeders’ buzzing. Damp air has ruined his metal woodworking tools, so he values the rust-resistant, sharp blades grown by marshfang slicers and is adapting them for handles. He supplies tradeskill goods and sees selling the blades as a promising sideline.

Magasha works at Swamprat Post and is tired of Reavij’s unwanted attention, which she says distracts him from his duties and leaves her cleaning up after him. She resents the endless mushroom meals and would rather eat fish; she is practical about earning coin, even when firefly wings do little for her fashion sense. She finds Reavij’s staring creepy and regrets that his assignment brought him to the post.

Seer Janidi studies the Feralfen’s carved totems for signs of their spirits, favoring the powerful serpent over the bird spirit he dismisses as weak and capricious. He hopes to bend the serpent spirit to his will, but its attack on the totem’s user convinces him that compelling it would take considerable effort; he turns instead to finding another source of power in Outland.

Fishing supplies in tow, Zurjaya is glad to find good fishing in Zangarmarsh, though Fenclaw Thrashers scare off fish and steal his bait. He resents being mocked by Gambarinka and wants to return with a proper catch. When a huge bogstrok breaks his line, he vows to pursue Terrorclaw; he also sets out to stop the persistent hydra Mragesh. Zurjaya treats these fishing frustrations as a personal rivalry and is determined to win by any means.

Timothy Daniels, known to friends as “the Specialist,” sells reagents and poison supplies at Orebor Harborage. He is absorbed by the Daggerfen Lost Ones’ specialized poison and investigates its recipe, objecting that ragveil has no toxic properties and is untrue to a rogue’s calling. He has an associate, Kialon, at Sylvanaar, and entrusts a private response letter to a courier, insisting it is for Kialon’s eyes alone.
Rajah Haghazed leads the Darkcrest naga, whom the Cenarion Expedition links to repeated attacks against its people. The Expedition has declared a bounty on him and considers him extremely dangerous.

Windcaller Blackhoof is a Cenarion Expedition figure concerned with the safety of its watchers, who document the marsh, gather samples and make contact with sentient peoples. He directs trusted allies to seek blessings from Ashyen and Keleth, ancients allied with the Expedition.

An Umbrafen Lost One of the tribe that Ikeyen describes as allied with the naga. The tribe uses dark magic to trap and enslave others, and Ikeyen fears its members would kill him if he left the refuge.

An Umbrafen Lost One of the tribe that Ikeyen describes as allied with the naga. The tribe uses dark magic to trap and enslave others, and Ikeyen fears its members would kill him if he left the refuge.

Kataru is named by Ikeyen as the leader of the Lost Ones of the Umbrafen tribe, described as cruel users of dark magic who trap and enslave others. Ikeyen calls for Kataru’s death at Umbrafen Village. In combat, Kataru uses Earth Shield and Chain Lightning.
Darkcrest Taskmasters are found in Zangarmarsh and use Tail Lash in combat.
Darkcrest Sirens use Frostbolt, Frost Nova and Silence in combat. When badly wounded, they flee for assistance.
Bloodscale Enchantresses of the Bloodscale Enclave are among the naga whose attacks on Sporeggar prompt calls to teach them a lesson. They use Arcane Missiles and Ice Barrier in combat.
Bloodscale Slavedrivers of the Bloodscale Enclave are targeted alongside the Enchantresses in Sporeggar’s response to continuing attacks on its people. They use Battle Shout when attacked.

Messenger Gazgrigg is an urgent courier serving the Mag’har command. His appeal sends help to Captain Kroghan in Garadar and warns that the settlement must not fall; the message directs the listener south through Nagrand to find the commander.
A Feralfen hunter in Zangarmarsh, this creature is equipped for ranged combat and summons a sporebat while out of combat.
A Feralfen mystic found in Zangarmarsh, this creature is equipped for combat.

A Daggerfen Lost One in Zangarmarsh, the Muckdweller is among the tribe’s organized, aggressive forces threatening roads and Zabra’jin. It uses paralytic poison in combat and may flee for help when badly wounded.
A Daggerfen Lost One in Zangarmarsh, the Assassin is among the tribe’s organized, aggressive forces threatening roads and Zabra’jin. It fights with toxic fumes.

An Ango’rosh ogre in the Hewn Bog, this member of the advancing force threatens a Kurenai refuge and the group’s effort to strengthen ties with Telredor. In combat it can become enraged and uses a kick.
An Ango'rosh ogre shaman of the Hewn Bog, this hostile spellcaster attacks with lightning. Ikuti's Kurenai mission identifies Ango'rosh shamans among the threats closing on the refuge.
An Ango'rosh brute in the Hewn Bog, this hostile ogre fights with knockdowns and can become enraged.
An Ango'rosh mauler of the Stronghold, this hostile ogre can unleash an overpowering strike when wounded. Zabra'jin's campaign names maulers among the Ango'rosh forces it seeks to defeat.

An Ango'rosh Souleater of the Stronghold, this hostile spellcaster hurls shadow bolts and can drain life when badly wounded. Zabra'jin's campaign counts Souleaters among the Ango'rosh forces it seeks to defeat.
A Dreghood Drudge encountered around the marsh, this hostile humanoid attacks intruders when they draw its attention.
A Wrekt Slave encountered around the marsh, this hostile humanoid responds to attack with Shared Bonds.

A fungal giant of the Dead Mire, this creature is withering as the soil loses moisture. Vindicator Idaar describes such giants as driven mad by their pain and beyond the draenei's ability to save; he asks that they be put out of their suffering.
A starving fungal giant found in the Dead Mire and nearby marshland. It attacks with choking vines, a threat that suits the overgrown wetlands it inhabits.
A bog lord of the Zangarmarsh wetlands, encountered in the marsh around the Dead Mire. It fights by striking with a forceful boglord bash.
Umbraglow Stingers are creatures of Zangarmarsh. They are encountered across the marsh and defend themselves with glowing blood.
Marshlight Bleeders are large, buzzing creatures found around Zangarmarsh. Their droning draws complaints from nearby residents, and they defend themselves with vibrant blood.
Fen Striders are creatures found across Zangarmarsh. In combat, they can use Lightning Tether.
Marsh Walkers inhabit the wetlands of Zangarmarsh. They are encountered in several marsh areas and can use Lightning Tether in combat.

Marsh Lurkers are among the marsh beasts that have recently invaded the sporelok caves of Funggor Cavern. Lauranna asks outsiders to clear the beasts from the area, placing these lurkers among the threats to the sporelok there.
Marsh Dredgers are marsh beasts encountered in Zangarmarsh, including Funggor Cavern. In combat, a Marsh Dredger can use strangling roots to hinder its foes.
A Sporeggar Preserver among the Sporeggar of Zangarmarsh.
A Sporeggar Harvester in the Sporeggar community of Zangarmarsh.
Gurgle is Tor'gash's pet, named alongside Gargle in Tor'gash's plan to introduce murlocs to the Lost Ones.
Gargle is Tor'gash's pet, named alongside Gurgle in Tor'gash's plan to introduce murlocs to the Lost Ones.
A young murloc intended for release among the Lost Ones at Daggerfen Village as part of Tor'gash's plan.
Boss Grog'ak oversees the Ango'rosh mushroom-cutting operation north of Zabra'jin. A wanted notice warns that his band may cut a path to the town if left unchecked.
Overlord Gorefist is the leader of the Ango'rosh. Two quests from different settlements name him as a target, with one describing his defeat as a way to disrupt the ogres' organization.

Elder Kuruti is addressed as an elder of the Feralfen. A draenei emissary is directed to speak with him in the guise of an arakkoa spirit, carrying a message that the draenei are ready to welcome his people as long-lost brothers and end their hostility.
Mudfin Frenzies are beasts found across two marsh areas.
Fenclaw Thrashers are animal creatures around Serpent Lake. They scare fish and snap bait from hooks, disrupting Zurjaya's fishing.
Lorti is a merchant who lets visitors browse his goods. His established role here is serving customers as a vendor.
Khalan is a stable master who helps visitors stable their pets and recover lost companions.
Merajit is an innkeeper who offers lodging and goods. Visitors may ask to rest at the inn or make it their home, alongside browsing his wares.
Tayemba is paired with Farbosi in an exchange of throws: Tayemba throws to Farbosi, who throws back to him. What they are throwing and what the exchange means are left unstated.
Farbosi is paired with Tayemba in an exchange of throws: Tayemba throws to Farbosi, who throws back to him. What they are throwing and what the exchange means are left unstated.
Joraal is a stable master who helps with pet stabling and lost companions. He offers these services through the stable at Telredor.
Caregiver Abidaar is an innkeeper in Zangarmarsh who welcomes visitors to sit and get comfortable.

Lord Klaq is identified as the leader of the marshbeasts attacking the Cenarion Expedition’s watchers near Funggor Cavern. Warden Hamoot believes killing him will end the attacks; Klaq is also described as using Thorns and Thunderclap in combat.
"Count" Ungula is a beast whose combat attacks include Tail Swipe.

Mragesh is a large hydra of Serpent Lake that has troubled anglers and nearly killed Maktu during a hunt for hides. Zurjaya calls him cunning and ferocious and wants to be the last angler he bothers. Maktu seeks revenge after narrowly escaping what he describes as the largest hydra he has seen.

Prospector Conall represents the Explorers' League in Zangarmarsh and refuses to be driven away by oversized insects. Conall seeks Blacksting's stinger to embarrass an earlier expedition and wants Sporewing killed to finish its abandoned work. Outshining the earlier prospectors is expected to earn a choice of assignments on returning to Ironforge.
Talut is a beast.
A steam pump overseer who threatens punishment for interference and warns that Warlord Kalithresh will hear of the intruder's insolence.
Sporeggar Spawn is a humanoid creature connected to Sporeggar.
Mycah is Sporeggar's quartermaster, offering goods to visitors who want to browse his wares.
Sal'salabim lists Coosh'coosh among his debtors. When confronted with a demand for payment, Coosh'coosh refuses and threatens the collector; he fights with lightning.
Marticar is a powerful named beast. It uses Magnetic Pull when engaged and casts Forked Lightning Tether on nearby foes.
The Coilfang Emissary is an elite creature bearing the Coilfang title; it uses Water Spout in combat.
The Bog Lurker is a powerful elemental that uses War Stomp when a target comes within close range.
Munci is a hippogryph master who handles flight travel. When threatened, Munci calls for help and summons an enraged hippogryph.
Du'ga is a wind rider master who handles flight travel. When threatened, Du'ga calls for guards and summons an enraged wyvern.
Coryth Stoktron is an innkeeper in Zangarmarsh, welcoming weary visitors to sit and rest. The inn offers lodging and goods; Coryth's greeting treats the visitor as a brother or sister.
Kerp is an innkeeper in Zangarmarsh who invites visitors to sit and get comfortable. The inn offers lodging and goods.
A Zabra'jin guard, serving as part of the settlement's defense.
A Swamprat guard who serves as one of the local defenders.
Juno Dufrain is a master fishing trainer who teaches fishing and also serves as a vendor.
Sporelok is a humanoid found in Terokkar Forest and Zangarmarsh.
A Telredor guard, serving as part of the settlement's defense.
A defender of Orebor Harborage, serving the settlement's protection.
Captain Krosh is a named figure in Outland. A Box of Mushrooms can be taken from him, and the item is sought for Watcher Leesa’oh’s effort to find a new food source for the bog lords.
Naka is a cooking trainer who also sells cooking supplies.

Chieftain Mummaki leads the Daggerfen Lost One tribe and a band described in wanted notices as assassins. The notices blame his group for lethal attacks on nearby settlements; in combat he can vanish when badly wounded.
Guard Untula orders someone to sharpen an axe and threatens to eat them if they cannot fix things.
A captured gnome who offers item repair and goods. In exchanges with Guard Untula, they say they do not understand him and plead not to be beaten, suggesting a frightened captive under his control.
A withered bog lord. Its combat behavior includes using Osmosis.
A starving bog lord found across several areas. Its combat behavior includes Choking Vines.
Loolruna is an armorer in Zangarmarsh. She offers both goods browsing and ammunition, alongside repair service, making her a practical stop for travelers maintaining their equipment.
Muheru the Weaver is a provider of tailoring supplies in Zangarmarsh.
Ango'rosh Warlocks are part of the hostile Ango'rosh presence in Zangarmarsh. These warlocks hold their ground outside combat, suggesting a guarded position rather than a roaming patrol.

Daggerfen Servants are humanoid combatants whose field behavior includes tending to wounded allies: when a nearby friendly is badly hurt, a servant can apply a bandage. This gives the group a practical support role alongside its combat presence.
Fungal Giants are large creatures whose combat behavior centers on hazardous fungi. A giant can throw a mushroom spore at its target and summon an unstable mushroom during a fight.
Darkcrest Slavers are humanoid combatants who use Demoralizing Shout against opponents.
Darkcrest Sorceresses are humanoid combatants who maintain Frost Armor while out of combat.
Doba is a named vendor whose cooking-supplies counter lets visitors browse goods.
Darkcrest Sentries are combatants with a watch role, as their name indicates. When badly hurt, a sentry may flee to seek assistance, revealing a defensive response under pressure.
Bloodscale Overseers are humanoid enemies found across the Outland marsh areas. This one uses Hamstring in combat.
A Bloodscale Wavecaller is a humanoid encountered in the marsh areas of Outland. It maintains Water Shield outside combat and casts Water Bolt in combat, marking it as a spell-using combatant.
Bloodscale Sentries are humanoid enemies found in several Outland marsh areas. When badly wounded, this sentry casts a spell.

Umbrafen Witchdoctors are among the Lost Ones of the Umbrafen tribe at Umbrafen Village, whom Ikeyen describes as users of dark magic who enslave others. This humanoid casts Shrink in combat; Ikeyen's quest names witchdoctors as targets.
Bloodthirsty Marshfangs are beasts found across the Outland marsh areas. This marshfang uses Drain Mana in combat.
Bogflare Needlers are beasts found in the Outland marsh areas. This needler uses Lambent Blood in combat.
A Fenglow Stinger is a stinging creature found in the Zangarmarsh area. It can release Glowing Blood during combat.
Feralfen druids are humanoids encountered in the Zangarmarsh wetlands. When attacked, a druid can assume Roc Form, reflecting its shapeshifting nature.
A Ragestone Threshalisk is a creature of the Zangarmarsh. It can feign death, then rise and charge forward; in combat it can also enter a frenzy.
A Ragestone Trampler is a creature of the Zangarmarsh. It can feign death, then rise and charge forward, and it uses Frenzy in combat.
A Marshrock Stomper is a creature found in the Zangarmarsh. It can feign death, then rise and charge forward; in combat it can use a stomping attack.
Lagoon Eels are found around a Zangarmarsh lagoon. An eel can use a combat ability when it becomes engaged.
Lagoon Walkers are humanoids found around a Zangarmarsh lagoon. They can use an ability when badly hurt in combat.
Marsh Baron Brok is a named marsh creature. When injured in combat, he can cast Wild Regeneration, giving him a way to recover under pressure.
Bogstrok Clackers are found among the marsh bogstrok. This clacker attacks on being engaged, marking it as an active combatant rather than a passive marsh creature.
Bogstrok Razorclaws are marsh bogstrok that fight with their claws; in combat, this one can inflict Gushing Wound, a threat beyond a simple claw strike.
Bogstrok Crushers are marsh bogstrok built for hard-hitting fights. This one can use Crush Armor in combat, setting it apart from the Razorclaw's wound-inflicting attack.
Parched Hydras inhabit the dry reaches of the marsh. In combat, this hydra can unleash Heat Wave, a striking danger in its parched surroundings.
Young sporebats are found across the marsh. When one dies, it releases Energizing Spores, leaving a final burst of its characteristic spores.
Captain Bo'kar is a named captain in the Marshlight Lake region.
An Ango'rosh sentry in the Marshlight Lake region, this combatant uses Cleave in combat.
An Ango'rosh Shadowmage in the Marshlight Lake region, this combatant uses Shadow Bolt and Shadow Shell in combat.
Mal'druk the Soulrender is a named figure in the Marshlight Lake region. In combat, Mal'druk casts Mind Flay and Summon Shadow Image below half health.

Terrorclaw is a named giant bogstrok of Marshlight Lake. Two local accounts seek its death for different reasons: one describes it as a naga taskmaster's pet used in a deadly game, while another tells of a fisherman's lost catch. Terrorclaw's own motives are not established by those accounts.
The Bogstrok Hatchling is a young bogstrok in the Marshlight Lake region.
Gur'zil is a wind rider master who handles flight inquiries. When attacked, he calls for guards.
Several Bloodscale Elementals are found in the Coilfang Reservoir area of Zangarmarsh.
Sarinei Whitestar is a general-goods vendor at Cenarion Refuge. She offers basic supplies and has a browse-goods option.
The Horde Air Force Trip Wire is a mechanical trip-wire device recorded at several locations across Outland.
The Air Force Alarm Bot is a mechanical alarm unit associated with Sporeggar and found in the surrounding Zangarmarsh area.
The Air Force Guard Post is a mechanical post associated with Sporeggar.
A rooftop trip wire designated for Sporeggar's air force.
An alarm bot assigned to the Cenarion air force.
A Cenarion air-force guard post identified with Stormcrow.

npcs.name: Air Force Trip Wire - Rooftop (Cenarion Expedition)

records.text: A rooftop trip wire designated for the Cenarion Expedition's air force.
Halu is a hippogryph master whose flightmaster menu offers flight destinations. When attacked, she calls for help and summons an enraged hippogryph.
Hch'uu says she feels lonely, wishes there were more children her age nearby, and sometimes misses the Shattrath City orphanage.

Morthis Whisperwing is a Druid of the Talon at Cenarion Refuge. He regards the Druids of the Talon as a legacy worth keeping: although they are no longer a formal group, he intends to remain one to the end of his days. He seeks an apprentice to pass on the secrets of the stormcrow and can prepare the rare Ward of Waking. His work also concerns Anzu, the powerful raven god; Morthis is relieved to learn the enemy's identity but considers the effort to confront him premature. After Anzu's defeat, he fears the god may try to return to Outland and urges continued vigilance.

Corvax is a named creature associated with Cenarion Refuge. Morthis Whisperwing names Corvax alongside Rook as enjoying freedom from earthbound responsibilities, a freedom Morthis envies while he completes a task before returning to the wing.

Rook is a named creature associated with Cenarion Refuge. Morthis Whisperwing names Rook alongside Corvax as enjoying freedom from earthbound responsibilities, a freedom Morthis envies while he completes a task before returning to the wing.
Mortog Steamhead says the Cenarion Expedition rescued him from certain death in the mines, and that he owes the group his life. He offers repair and reagent services to allies of the Expedition.

The Alliance-aligned Zangarmarsh Flame Warden speaks for the Alliance festival fires. He encourages honoring fires in Alliance settlements and desecrating Horde fires, framing the opposing effort as unworthy.

The Horde-aligned Zangarmarsh Flame Keeper speaks for the Horde festival fires. She encourages honoring fires in Horde settlements and desecrating Alliance fires, framing the opposing effort as unworthy.

place_records.text: You are in Zangarmarsh, a contested marsh in Outland where the Alliance and the Horde both hold settlements. Telredor and Orebor Harborage are Alliance towns, Zabra'jin is Horde, and Cenarion Refuge is kept by neither side. It is a land of lakes, bogs and mires. Its main dangers are Bloodscale naga, fungal giants and bog lords, and the Lost One tribes such as the Daggerfen, who fight for control of the roads.

You are in Cenarion Refuge, the base of the Cenarion Expedition in Zangarmarsh, and neither the Alliance nor the Horde holds it. Expedition leader Ysiel Windsinger studies the marsh as its lakes lose water, while druid Lethyn Moonfire works to keep the marsh in balance. The Ancients Ashyen and Keleth offer their blessings to trusted allies. Its inn and stable are the place to rest and to recover lost pets.

You are in Daggerfen Village, a village of the Daggerfen Lost Ones in Zangarmarsh. Daggerfen muckdwellers and assassins are the dangers here, and Chieftain Mummaki leads them. Witch Doctor Tor'gash of Zabra'jin plans to release murlocs among the Lost Ones here.

You are in Umbrafen Village, a village of the Umbrafen tribe in Zangarmarsh. Umbrafen oracles, seers and witchdoctors haunt it, and Kataru leads them. Druid Kayra Longmane was abducted from near Cenarion Refuge and is trying to escape from here.

You are in Feralfen Village, home of the Feralfen Lost Ones in Zangarmarsh. Feralfen hunters, mystics and druids are the dangers here, and a fen strider and a blacksting roam nearby. The Feralfen have turned back to worship of animal spirits, and Alliance and Horde scholars want their carved idols studied.

You are in Bloodscale Enclave, a naga stronghold in Zangarmarsh. Bloodscale slavedrivers and enchantresses keep wrekt slaves at work here, and sentries watch the approaches. Naga of the enclave are reported to be killing Sporeggar's people.

You are in Telredor, an Alliance refuge of draenei in Zangarmarsh. Anchorite Ahuurn turned an old shrine here into a haven, and he hopes to reunite the Lost Ones with the draenei. Vindicator Idaar tests the depleted soil of the Dead Mire. Its inn and repairs serve the Alliance.

You are in Zabra'jin, a Horde outpost in Zangarmarsh that Shadow Hunter Denjai oversees for the Darkspear forces. Denjai suspects that ogres from the Ango'rosh grounds are staging an attack, and ogres are filtering down from the northern mountains. Its inn, stable and flight point serve Horde travelers.
You are in Quagg Ridge, a ridge in Zangarmarsh where fungal giants and bog lords are the main dangers. Starving fungal giants and starving bog lords roam here as well.

You are in The Spawning Glen, a glen in Zangarmarsh where the Sporelings raise their young. Fahssn speaks for them there, pleading for help as fungal giants devour their spore sacs. Starving fungal giants and starving bog lords roam the glen, and a marticar is also here.

You are in the Dead Mire, a withered stretch of Zangarmarsh where the fungus and the soil are dying. Withered giants, withered bog lords, marshrock threshaliks and parched hydras roam it. A broken steam pump sits in the mire, and Horde scout Jyoba was found dead here with his report missing.

You are in Sporeggar, a village of Sporelings in Zangarmarsh. Its primus Msshi'fn keeps the village supplied, and its people trade glowcap mushrooms for food. Sanguine hibiscus has grown scarce as the marsh dries, and the Sporelings are at war with the spore giants. The marsh walkers are an old enemy, and the Black Stalker is their great mother.

You are in Ango'rosh Grounds, an ogre camp in Zangarmarsh northwest of Zabra'jin. Ango'rosh sentries, brutes, warlocks and maulers keep watch here, and marshlight bleeders drift through the camp. Shadow Hunter Denjai suspects the ogres are preparing an attack on Zabra'jin.

You are in Ango'rosh Stronghold, an ogre hold in a cave on a small island in Zangarmarsh, reached over a fallen mushroom. Ango'rosh ogres led by Overlord Gorefist keep it, and Mal'druk the Soulrender is among them. Maulers, souleaters and shadowmages make the cave dangerous.
You are in Funggor Cavern, a cavern in Zangarmarsh. Marsh lurkers and marsh dredgers are its dangers. Sporelok, a humanoid also found in Terokkar Forest, can be met here.

You are in Serpent Lake, a lake in Zangarmarsh. Cenarion Expedition investigator Watcher Jhang is looking for four missing companions, and Mortog Steamhead, who says the Expedition saved him from the mines, offers repairs and reagents to its allies. Mudfin frenzies, fenclaw thrashers, and Bloodscale overseers and wavecallers are its dangers.

You are in Umbrafen Lake, a lake in Zangarmarsh. Umbrafen eels are its main danger, with mire hydras, darkcrest sorceresses and umbraglow stingers also about. A gas cloud called Swamp Gas is found here.

You are in Marshlight Lake, a lake in Zangarmarsh. Bogstrok crushers, bogstrok razorclaws and bogstrok hatchlings are its dangers, along with bloodscale enchantresses, bloodscale slavedrivers and marshlight bleeders. Swamp Gas, a gas cloud, is found here.
You are in Sporewind Lake, a lake in Zangarmarsh. Bogstrok hatchlings and bogstrok clackers are its main dangers.

You are in The Lagoon, a lagoon in Zangarmarsh. Lagoon eels and lagoon walkers are its main dangers, with mire hydras, bloodthirsty marshfangs and Marsh Baron Brok also about. Young sporebats are found here, and when one dies it releases a burst of spores.

You are in Hewn Bog, a bog in Zangarmarsh. Ango'rosh ogres and their shamans are its main dangers, and the ogres have cleared the bog of its towering mushrooms. Marsh walkers and marshlight bleeders are also about.

You are in Swamprat Post, a Horde outpost in Zangarmarsh. Zurai, a merchant and outpost leader sent by Shadow Hunter Denjai, runs it, and Gur'zil the wind rider master handles flights from here. Scout Jyoba has not returned from the Dead Mire, and marshfang rippers crawl around the post.

You are in Twin Spire Ruins, ruins in Zangarmarsh where a spirit healer offers a return to life for a price. Mudfin frenzies, bloodthirsty marshfangs and fen striders are its dangers, with fenclaw thrashers and marshfang slicers also about.

You are in Orebor Harborage, an Alliance refuge in Zangarmarsh where a Kurenai delegation led by Ikuti defends the place from Ango'rosh ogres. Halu, the hippogryph master, handles flights here, and Timothy Daniels, known as the Specialist, is busy studying Daggerfen poison.

You are in Bloodscale Grounds, a stretch of Zangarmarsh where bloodscale overseers, wavecallers, sentries and elementals are the dangers. Steam pump overseers and wrekt slaves are about too, and the steam pumps here are used to drain the water from the marsh.

You are in Darkcrest Enclave, in Zangarmarsh. Darkcrest taskmasters, sirens and sentries prowl the ground here, Dreghood drudges are common too, and Coilfang emissaries are seen now and then. Umbraglow stingers are a danger here as well.

You are in Darkcrest Shore, on the edge of Zangarmarsh. Dreghood drudges, Darkcrest slavers and Darkcrest sorceresses roam here, with Darkcrest sentries, Umbraglow stingers and Mire hydras as further dangers.

You are in Cenarion Watchpost, in Zangarmarsh. Watcher Leesa'oh studies the sporelings here and watches how they live alongside the marsh's other creatures. Hungry bog lords are eating the sporelings' pods, and she fears they may wipe the sporelings out. Buddy, her animal companion, follows her about.
